headline: Science Student Wins National Space Day Competition By Submitting Detailed Map Of His Own Lost Keys
body:
The celebrations for National Space Day 2026 at the Institute of Science in Mumbai reached an unexpected climax yesterday when a second-year physics student was awarded the top prize for 'Excellence in Mapping Uncharted Territories.' The judges confirmed that the winning entry, a sprawling, hand-drawn cartography of the student’s own apartment floor, was the only submission that successfully documented the exact coordinates of his keys, which had been missing since mid-July.

“We were looking for deep space observation logs, but the precision with which he located his key ring behind a stack of lukewarm thermoses was frankly extraterrestrial,” said Dr. V. Rajan, the event’s lead coordinator. “Mapping a space where nothing is ever found is a far greater scientific achievement than documenting a nebula that doesn’t even have a mortgage to worry about.”

For the winning student, the breakthrough came after he applied principles of dark matter and quantum entanglement to his living room sofa. “I realized that the keys weren't lost; they had simply entered a sub-space dimension between the cushion and the wooden frame,” he explained while accepting a commemorative plaque that he immediately misplaced. “If I can calculate the trajectory of my missing car keys, I’m confident I can solve the mysteries of the cosmos by next semester.”

Following the announcement, the university administration has reportedly received forty-two similar entries from students claiming to have mapped the precise locations of their lost socks, misplaced textbooks, and the remnants of their own academic ambition, all of which will now be filed under the Institute’s official 'Hidden Reality' research initiative.
caption: Physics student wins top honors at National Space Day for finding his keys instead of a planet. Is your living room the final frontier? #NationalSpaceDay #MumbaiScience #AcademicLife #LostAndFound (satire)
